subject: Reference program: CS guardrails (reference load, escalation path, HubSpot logging)

body:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>, Miguel Santos <miguel_santos@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>, Tyler Benson <tyler_benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Oct 15, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Reference program: CS guardrails (reference load, escalation path, HubSpot logging)

Team — sharing CS guardrails for the customer reference program so we can move fast without burning goodwill.

1) Reference load limits (default)
- Reference calls: max 2 per month per customer reference contact (unless explicitly approved by CSM + customer).
- Case study work: treat interviews/review cycles as “reference load” too. If a customer is in drafting/approval for a public story, pause new reference-call asks unless it’s a true late-stage exec escalation.
- Cooldown: if a customer signals fatigue OR we have any friction (missed prep, scope creep, repeated reschedules), we put them on a 30-day cooldown and route all new requests through the CSM.

2) No-surprise policy
- AEs/SEs should not email customers directly with a reference request unless the CSM has confirmed (a) the ask is appropriate and (b) the customer is expecting it.
- Marketing will coordinate for public assets (logo/quote/case study) but CS owns relationship readiness.

3) Escalation path if customer discomfort arises
If the customer expresses discomfort (or even mild “we’re getting too many asks”):
- Step 1: Stop the request immediately and thank them. Do not negotiate on the call.
- Step 2: CSM follows up within 24 hours to reset expectations and confirm boundaries.
- Step 3: Notify in Slack #customer-references with a short note (customer, what happened, current status).
- Step 4: If there are contractual/compliance concerns (NDA scope, metric disclosure, security wording), loop Legal owner (Michael Grant) via Camila.
- Step 5: If it’s a high-stakes deal pressure situation, route to exec sponsor (Stephanie) only after CS/Marketing alignment.

4) What must be logged back to HubSpot (required)
We cannot measure impact or prevent overuse without consistent logging.
For every reference call request (even if it doesn’t happen), log:
- Requestor (AE/SE/CSM)
- Prospect + deal link (if applicable)
- Customer reference requested
- Outcome: scheduled / completed / declined / postponed
- Date of call (or decline date)
- Notes: top Qs asked + any “avoid list” items that came up
- Reference load update: increment monthly count and set next eligible date if needed

Tyler is setting up the properties + a simple workflow so this is ~2 minutes of work, not a chore. Until that’s live, please drop outcomes in #customer-references and tag Tyler so he can backfill.

5) Prep expectations (to reduce friction)
- AEs must provide the reference-call brief (1 pager) at least 2 business days before the call.
- Include: what to emphasize, what to avoid, and the prospect’s top 3 questions.
- If we don’t have the brief in time, we reschedule. This is non-negotiable — it’s how we keep customers willing.

Camila — feel free to lift this into the broader playbook / enablement doc.

Thanks,
Jasmine
—
Jasmine Liu
Customer Success Ops
Redwood Inference


On Wed, Oct 15, 2025 at 9:34 AM Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> +1. Especially the “no-surprise” policy and the cooldown. We’ve had a couple customers quietly get annoyed rather than say no outright.
> 
> Can we add one more explicit guardrail: if a customer is within 2 weeks of a renewal / active escalation, we don’t ask for references unless the CSM says it’s appropriate?


From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Miguel Santos <miguel_santos@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>, Tyler Benson <tyler_benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Oct 15, 2025 at 9:47 AM
Subject: Re: Reference program: CS guardrails (reference load, escalation path, HubSpot logging)

Yes — great call. I’ll add:
- “No reference asks within 14 days of renewal signature date OR during an active escalation, unless CSM explicitly greenlights.”

Miguel: can you sanity-check this against what you’re seeing with Northwind/Helios (re: review windows + load)?


On Wed, Oct 15, 2025 at 10:22 AM Miguel Santos <miguel_santos@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Looks good. Northwind was fine with 1 call + the draft review in the same month, but only because we prepped them and kept it tight.
> 
> Helios is the opposite — longer legal/compliance loops + fewer spokespeople. For them I’d recommend max 1 reference call/month, period, and keep it to their named approvers.
> 
> Also +1 to the “reschedule without a brief” rule. Customers can tell when we’re winging it.


From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Miguel Santos <miguel_santos@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>, Tyler Benson <tyler_benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Oct 15, 2025 at 11:03 AM
Subject: Re: Reference program: CS guardrails (reference load, escalation path, HubSpot logging)

Perfect — let’s treat “max 1 call/month” as the default for regulated / approvals-heavy customers (Helios-type) unless they proactively opt into more.

Tyler — once properties are live, can we add a simple “Reference Tier” dropdown (Standard vs Regulated/Approvals-heavy) so the workflow can enforce the limit and flag overages?

Camila/Avery — if you’re OK with it, I’ll repost the final guardrails in #customer-references and we’ll pin.

Jasmine
